Its factually correct, both in humans and plants. Hybrids are created by crossing two plants with desirable traits. Repetitive pre-breeding of those two parent plants insures that all the seeds have (nearly) identical genetics. This is called "homozygosity."

When both parents have the same harmful recessive genes, its extremely likely that they will be dominant in the offspring, therefore seeds are generally not viable. When hybridized offspring are viable, they tend to manifest all the traits that were selected against in their parents. Because most hybrids are optimized for fast growth, if the "fast growth gene" (it's more the one gene, but for the sake of simplicity) goes recessive. The objective result is that the plant's growth is literally retarded.
